themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often shifts while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers call the assistants nondeterministic with no stable denominator, cross-channel incrementality answers say platforms change delivery mid-test, identity resolution answers say confidence scores are unverified without a truth set, and the B2B buying-group and content governance answers both note that even expert reviewers and closed-won records give biased or missing labels.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The models increasingly try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers propose a fast lane with perks so declaring beats spoofing, journey orchestration answers say channel owners paid on their own conversions will subvert a central arbiter, the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions an entrenched political fight rather than a data problem, and incrementality answers note platforms have no reason to expose auditable treatment logs.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every agent execution answer routes writes through a proxy or gateway with spend, rate, and audience caps because sends and spend have no rollback, the downstream consent answers put a single checkpoint on every path data leaves the warehouse, and the orchestration answers require all channels to call one shared pre-send check.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from the outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: The downstream consent answers call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes and say deletion from a trained model has no accepted test, the incrementality answers say platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and the answer engine answers say there are no ranking logs or source lineage to inspect.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Content governance answers all build a registry of pre-approved claims and evidence and then admit that deciding whether wording crosses a line stays a human call, and the semantic context layer answers argue two teams can both be right about what revenue means, so the goal is forced disclosure of which definition was used rather than one true definition.
